The '''Ballon d'Or''' ({{IPA|fr|balɔ̃ dɔʁ|-|LL-Q150 (fra)-Touam-Ballon d'Or.wav}}; {{lit|'''Golden Ball'''}}) is an annual [[association football]] award presented by French magazine ''[[France Football]]'' since [[1956 Ballon d'Or|1956]] to honour the [[football player|player]] judged to have performed the best over the previous [[Season (sports)|season]].

Conceived by sports writers [[Gabriel Hanot]] and [[Jacques Ferran]], the Ballon d'Or was based exclusively on voting by football journalists up until [[2006 Ballon d'Or|2006]]. Originally, it was awarded only to players from Europe and was also known as the '''European Footballer of the Year''' award. In [[1995 Ballon d'Or|1995]], the Ballon d'Or was expanded to include all players of any origin active at European clubs. The award became a global prize in [[2007 Ballon d'Or|2007]] with all professional footballers being eligible; additionally, coaches and captains of national teams were also given the right to vote, before reverting to just journalists in [[2016 Ballon d'Or|2016]].

Between [[2010 FIFA Ballon d'Or|2010]] and [[2015 FIFA Ballon d'Or|2015]], in an agreement with [[FIFA]], the award was merged with the [[FIFA World Player of the Year]] and rebranded as the [[FIFA Ballon d'Or]]. That partnership ended in 2016, and the award reverted to the Ballon d'Or, while FIFA also reinstated its own separate annual award, [[The Best FIFA Men's Player]]. In [[2022 Ballon d'Or|2022]], ''France Football'' modified the rules for the Ballon d'Or. The timing was changed so that the award is based on a football season rather than a calendar year, and an international jury of specialized journalists—one representative per country from the top 100 in the latest [[FIFA Men's World Ranking]]—was introduced to determine the winner. [[UEFA]] has co-organized the Ballon d'Or gala since [[2024 Ballon d'Or|2024]], with ''France Football'' retaining the voting system and the Ballon d'Or name.

[[Lionel Messi]] has won the Ballon d'Or a record eight times, followed by [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] with five. [[Johan Cruyff]], [[Michel Platini]] and [[Marco van Basten]] have each won the award three times, while [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]], [[Franz Beckenbauer]], [[Kevin Keegan]], [[Karl-Heinz Rummenigge]] and [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] have each won it twice. [[Ousmane Dembélé]] is the current holder of the award, having won [[2025 Ballon d'Or|its 69th edition]] in 2025.
{{TOC limit|3}}

== Overview ==
[[File:1956 France Football magazine cover.jpg|left|thumb|upright|December 1956 issue of ''[[France Football]]'' magazine presenting the [[1956 Ballon d'Or|inaugural Ballon d'Or]] winner—[[Stanley Matthews]].]]
The Ballon d'Or is widely regarded as the most prestigious individual award in football.<ref name="DiarioAS2023" /><ref name="Goal2023" /><ref name="TheSportingNews2025" /> Prior to [[2007 Ballon d'Or|2007]], it was based exclusively on voting by football journalists and was also known as the continental European Footballer of the Year award.<ref name="WorldSoccer2007" /><ref name="PerspectivesonPolitics2020" /> Even after 2007, it was usually identified with and referred to by that name because of its origin as a European award,<ref name="BBCSport2008a" /><ref name="TheTelegraph2008" /> until it was merged with the [[FIFA World Player of the Year]] award cementing its new worldwide claim.<ref name="TheGuardian2007" /><ref name="FIFA2009" /> [[Stanley Matthews]] of England was the [[1956 Ballon d'Or|inaugural winner]] of the award, and the oldest player to ever win it—at {{ayd|1915|2|1|1956|12|18}} old.<ref name="UEFA2025" /><ref name="BBCSport2008b" />

Liberia's [[George Weah]], the only African recipient, became the first non-European to win the award in [[1995 Ballon d'Or|1995]], the year that rules of eligibility were changed and the Ballon d'Or was expanded to include all players of any origin active at European clubs;<ref name="BBCSport2008c" /><ref name="NBCSports2023" /> [[1997 Ballon d'Or|two years later]], [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] of Brazil became the first South American without a European citizenship to claim the award,<ref name="BBCSport2008c" /> and he is still the youngest winner ever at {{ayd|1976|9|18|1997|12|23}} old.<ref name="ESPN2023" /> The award became a global prize in 2007 with all professional footballers from clubs around the world being eligible;<ref name="BBCSport2008d" /> additionally, coaches and captains of national teams were also given the right to vote,<ref name="PerspectivesonPolitics2020" /><ref name="ESPN2023" /> before reverting to just journalists in [[2016 Ballon d'Or|2016]].<ref name="TheAthletic2023a" /><ref name="BBCSport2025" />

[[File:Milan AC - Gianni Rivera - Ballon d'Or 1969.jpg|thumb|upright|[[Gianni Rivera]] hoisting the [[1969 Ballon d'Or]].]]
[[Lionel Messi]] holds the record for most Ballon d'Or wins with eight,<ref name="GuinnessWorldRecords2023" /><ref name="Reuters2023" /><ref name="LeParisien2023" /> while five-time winner [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] earned the most nominations with eighteen.<ref name="IOC2025" /> Messi is the only player to win the award with three clubs and also the only one to win it while playing outside Europe,<ref name="TheNewYorkTimes2023" /><ref name="TheAthletic2023b" /> as well as being the player with the most [[podium]]s, finishing in the top-three a record fourteen times, including eleven consecutive from 2007 to 2017.<ref name="Reuters2023" /> Three players have won the award three times each: [[Johan Cruyff]], [[Michel Platini]] and [[Marco van Basten]].<ref name="UEFA2025" /><ref name="IOC2025" /> With seven awards each, Dutch, German, and Portuguese players have won the second most Ballons d'Or, underneath Argentina and France in first with eight.<ref name="NBCSports2023" />

Players from [[West Germany]] ([[1972 Ballon d'Or|1972]], [[1981 Ballon d'Or|1981]]) and the Netherlands ([[1988 Ballon d'Or|1988]]) occupied the top-three spots in a single year. West German (1972) and Italian (1988–[[1990 Ballon d'Or|1990]]) clubs achieved the same feat, including two individual years dominated by [[AC Milan|Milan]] players (1988, [[1989 Ballon d'Or|1989]]), a unique record until Spanish clubs experienced an unprecedented dominance ([[2009 Ballon d'Or|2009]]–[[2012 FIFA Ballon d'Or|2012]], [[2015 FIFA Ballon d'Or|2015]], 2016) and [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] ([[2010 FIFA Ballon d'Or|2010]]) became the second club to occupy the top-three.<ref name="LeParisien2023" /> The award shows a bias in favour of attacking players,<ref name="BleacherReport2015" /> and, over time, it has gone to a more exclusive set of leagues and clubs.<ref name="PerspectivesonPolitics2020" /> Prior to 1995, ten leagues supplied Ballon d'Or winners, whereas only England, France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the United States have supplied winners since then.<ref name="PerspectivesonPolitics2020" /><ref name="Goal2022a" /> Spain's [[La Liga]] has the most Ballon d'Or winners overall, with twenty-four wins shared between Barcelona and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]; with twelve wins each,<ref name="SportsIllustrated2025a" /> the two Spanish clubs also lead the overall club ranking for producing the most winners.<ref name="Goal2022a" /><ref name="RSSSF2025" />

Between 2010 and 2015 inclusive, the award was merged with a similar one, the FIFA World Player of the Year award, to create the [[FIFA Ballon d'Or]],<ref name="BBCSport2025" /><ref name="FIFA2010" /> which was awarded to the world's best male player before FIFA and ''[[France Football]]'' decided not to continue the merging agreement.<ref name="DiarioAS2023" /><ref name="ESPN2023" /> The recipients of the joint FIFA Ballon d'Or are considered as winners by both award organizations.<ref name="PerspectivesonPolitics2020" /><ref name="LEquipe2023" /><ref name="FIFA2024" /> In 2020, [[Groupe Amaury]], to which ''France Football'' belongs,<ref name="UEFA2023" /> decided that no award would be given for the year due to the [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on association football]].<ref name="ESPN2020" /><ref name="FranceFootball2020a" /> It has been widely argued that the 2020 Ballon d'Or would likely have been awarded to [[Robert Lewandowski]].<ref name="Forbes2020" /><ref name="ESPN2021" /><ref name="Marca2021" />

''France Football'' modified the rules for the Ballon d'Or in [[2022 Ballon d'Or|2022]].<ref name="BBCSport2025" /> They changed the timing so that awards were given not for achievements during a calendar year, but for a football season.<ref name="ESPN2023" /><ref name="LEquipe2022" /> It was also decided that an international jury of specialized journalists, with one representative per country, from the top 100 in the latest [[FIFA Men's World Ranking]] would determine the winner of the award;<ref name="TheAthletic2023a" /><ref name="UEFA2024" /> the plebiscite had previously been open to all countries since 2007.<ref name="ESPN2023" /><ref name="LEquipe2022" /> [[UEFA]] co-organizes the Ballon d'Or gala, a role it has held since [[2024 Ballon d'Or|2024]], with ''France Football'' retaining the voting system and the Ballon d'Or name.<ref name="UEFA2023" /><ref name="LeFigaro2023" />

=== Criteria ===
The Ballon d'Or is awarded based on three main criteria:<ref name="BBCSport2025" /><ref name="UEFA2024" />
:1) Individual performances, decisive and impressive character;
:2) Team performances and achievements;
:3) Class and fair play.
Nevertheless, critics have occasionally described the award as a "popularity contest",<ref name="OptusSport2023" /><ref name="Marca2016" /> criticizing its voting process,<ref name="TheAthletic2023a" /> its bias in favour of attacking players,<ref name="BleacherReport2015" /> and the idea of systematically singling out an individual in a team sport.<ref name="TheGuardian2008" /><ref name="BleacherReport2016" />

== Winners ==
[[File:Lionel-Messi-Argentina-2022-FIFA-World-Cup (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|[[Lionel Messi]] has won a record eight Ballons d'Or across three different decades, and holds the record for most consecutive wins, with four between [[2009 Ballon d'Or|2009]] and [[2012 FIFA Ballon d'Or|2012]].]]
[[File:Cristiano Ronaldo WC2022 - 01 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|[[Cristiano Ronaldo]] has been nominated for the Ballon d'Or a record eighteen times and is a five-time winner.]]
[[File:Stanley Matthews 1962 (crop).jpg|thumb|upright|[[Stanley Matthews]] was the inaugural recipient and remains the oldest winner of the award, aged {{ayd|1915|2|1|1956|12|18}}.]]
[[File:Luis Suárez Miramontes.JPG|thumb|upright|[[Luis Suárez (footballer, born 1935)|Luis Suárez]] was the first midfielder to win the award.]]
[[File:LevYashin.JPG|thumb|upright|[[Lev Yashin]] is the only goalkeeper to have won the award.]]
[[File:Johan Cruijff (1974).jpg|thumb|upright|[[Johan Cruyff]] was the first player to win the award three times.]]
[[File:Franz Beckenbauer (1975).jpg|thumb|upright|[[Franz Beckenbauer]] is the only defender to have won the award twice.]]
[[File:President George Weah in 2019 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|[[George Weah]]—the only African recipient—was the first non-European to win the award.]]
[[File:Ronaldo 2002 cropped.jpg|thumb|upright|Two-time winner [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] was the first South American to win the award and remains the youngest recipient, aged {{ayd|1976|9|18|1997|12|23}}.]]
[[File:Ousmane Dembele France v Senegal 16 June 2026-341 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|[[Ousmane Dembélé]] is the current award holder.]]
'''Note:''' Until [[2021 Ballon d'Or|2021]], the Ballon d'Or was awarded based on player performance during the calendar year. Since [[2022 Ballon d'Or|2022]], jurors have been instructed to take into account the previous season.<ref name="DiarioAS2023" /><ref name="LEquipe2022" />

== Additional awards ==
=== Seasonal awards ===
[[File:25th Laureus World Sports Awards - 240422 214032.jpg|thumb|upright|[[Aitana Bonmatí]] won the [[Ballon d'Or Féminin]] a record three times and in consecutive years, from [[2023 Ballon d'Or#Ballon d'Or Féminin|2023]] to [[2025 Ballon d'Or#Ballon d'Or Féminin|2025]].]]
In addition to the Ballon d'Or award, ''[[France Football]]'' has introduced several complementary honours over the years to recognize excellence across different aspects of the game.<ref name="TheSportingNews2025" /><ref name="SportsIllustrated2025b" />

=== Special awards ===
[[File:Pele con brasil (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|[[Pelé]] was voted Football Player of the Century in 1999. He was also the recipient of the FIFA Ballon d'Or Prix d'Honneur in 2013, and in 2020 he was selected to the [[Ballon d'Or Dream Team]].]]
[[File:Maradona-Mundial 86 con la copa.JPG|thumb|upright|[[Diego Maradona]] was honoured with the Golden Ballon d'Or in 1995 and he was also selected to the [[Ballon d'Or Dream Team]].]]
In addition to its annual awards, the Ballon d'Or has also been associated with a number of special and honorary distinctions, introduced on specific occasions to commemorate milestones, recognize all-time greatness, or address historical limitations of the award.<ref name="TheAthletic2023a" /><ref name="FranceFootball2020c" />

==== Super Ballon d'Or ====
{{Main|Super Ballon d'Or}}
[[File:Di Stefano 1959.jpg|thumb|upright|Two-time Ballon d'Or winner [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]], recipient of the [[Super Ballon d'Or]] in 1989.]]
The '''Super Ballon d'Or''' is an honorary award presented to [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]] in 1989,<ref name="TheAthletic2023a" /> who was voted the greatest multiple-time Ballon d'Or winner ahead of [[Johan Cruyff]] and [[Michel Platini]].<ref name="SPORTbible2022" /><ref name="TheSportingNews2023" />

Additionally, other honorary distinctions have been awarded in connection with the Ballon d'Or. [[Diego Maradona]] received an honorary award in 1995, referred to as the '''Golden Ballon d'Or''', in recognition of his services to football.<ref name="TheAthletic2023a" /><ref name="SPORTbible2022" /><ref name="FranceFootball2020b" /> [[Pelé]] received a similar honour during the [[2013 FIFA Ballon d'Or]] ceremony, known as the '''FIFA Ballon d'Or Prix d'Honneur'''.<ref name="TheAthletic2023a" /><ref name="FIFA2014" />

==== Football Player of the Century ====
In 1999, ''France Football'' voted [[Pelé]] as the '''Football Player of the Century''' after consulting their former Ballon d'Or recipients.<ref name="TheAthletic2023a" /> Among the 34 previous winners, 30 cast their votes, while [[Stanley Matthews]], [[Omar Sívori]] and [[George Best]] refused to vote, and [[Lev Yashin]] had died. Each voter was allotted five votes worth up to five points; however, Di Stéfano only chose a first place, Platini a first and second place, and [[George Weah]] two players for fifth place. Pelé was named the greatest by 17 voters, receiving almost double the number of points earned by the second place, [[Diego Maradona]].<ref name="RSSSF2015" />

==== ''Le nouveau palmarès'' ====
To coincide with the 60th anniversary of the Ballon d'Or in [[2016 Ballon d'Or|2016]], ''France Football'' published an internationalized reevaluation of the awards presented before [[1995 Ballon d'Or|1995]], when only European players were eligible to win the award.<ref name="TheAthletic2023a" /><ref name="FranceFootball2020b" /> 12 out of the 39 Ballons d'Or presented during this time period would have been awarded to South American players; in addition to Pelé—seven times—and Diego Maradona—twice—[[Garrincha]], [[Mario Kempes]], and [[Romário]] were retrospectively recognized as worthy winners.<ref name="FranceFootball2020b" /><ref name="FranceFootball2015" /> The original recipients, however, remain unchanged.<ref name="Goal2023" />
